### Expected Behavior

When the selected target file already exists, the Windows overwrite confirmation should remain visible until the user confirms or cancels the operation.

### Actual Behavior

The Windows overwrite confirmation appears and is dismissed automatically without user input. The existing target file is not locked by another process.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd00a3aa-e650-4e3d-8b7e-8f39b6d4cbb5

### Testcase Gist URL

A standalone testcase is provided as a ZIP attachment.

**Testcase ZIP:** [electron-save-dialog-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30568973/electron-save-dialog-repro.zip)

1. Extract the ZIP file.
2. Run `pnpm install`, then `pnpm start`.
3. Click **Show save dialog**.
4. Keep the default filename, click **Save**, and observe the overwrite confirmation.

Minimal source:

`package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "electron-save-dialog-sharing-violation-repro",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "main": "main.js",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "electron ."
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "electron": "42.7.1"
  }
}
```

`main.js`:

```js
const { app, dialog } = require("electron");
const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  const target = path.join(app.getPath("downloads"), "electron-save-dialog-repro.zip");
  fs.writeFileSync(target, "overwrite confirmation reproduction\r\n");
  const result = await dialog.showSaveDialog({
    defaultPath: target,
    filters: [{ name: "ZIP archive", extensions: ["zip"] }]
  });
  console.log(result);
  fs.rmSync(target, { force: true });
  app.quit();
});
```

### Additional Information

Microsoft documents that the Common Item Dialog displays an overwrite confirmation by default:

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog#onshareviolation-and-onoverwrite

Electron's Windows implementation creates `IFileSaveDialog` with `FOS_OVERWRITEPROMPT`:

https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_win.cc

### Expected Behavior

When the selected existing file is exclusively locked by another process, the save dialog should report the sharing violation, remain open, and require the user to choose another destination. This matches the default behavior documented for the Windows Common Item Dialog.

### Actual Behavior

The Windows overwrite confirmation appears and is dismissed automatically. The save operation cannot proceed normally, and the user cannot use the standard save dialog to resolve the sharing violation.

The behavior is identical with:

- `dialog.showSaveDialog()` without a parent window
- `dialog.showSaveDialog()` with a parent window
- `dialog.showSaveDialogSync()`
- Electron's `DownloadItem` save dialog
- Chromium's File System Access save picker in Electron

### Testcase Gist URL

The authenticated GitHub token cannot create gists, so the complete minimal testcase is included below.

`package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "electron-save-dialog-sharing-violation-repro",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "private": true,
  "main": "main.js",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "electron ."
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "electron": "42.7.1"
  }
}
```

`main.js`:

```js
const { app, dialog } = require("electron");
const { spawn } = require("node:child_process");
const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");

let locker;

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  const target = path.join(app.getPath("downloads"), "electron-save-dialog-repro.zip");
  fs.writeFileSync(target, "sharing violation reproduction\r\n");

  locker = spawn("python", ["-u", path.join(__dirname, "lock-file.py"), target], {
    stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "inherit"],
    windowsHide: true
  });
  locker.stdout.once("data", async () => {
    console.log(`Exclusively locked: ${target}`);
    const result = await dialog.showSaveDialog({
      defaultPath: target,
      filters: [{ name: "ZIP archive", extensions: ["zip"] }]
    });
    console.log(result);
    locker.stdin.end();
    app.quit();
  });
});

app.on("before-quit", () => locker?.stdin.end());
```

`lock-file.py`:

```python
import ctypes
import sys
from ctypes import wintypes

GENERIC_READ = 0x80000000
GENERIC_WRITE = 0x40000000
OPEN_ALWAYS = 4
FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL = 0x80
INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE = ctypes.c_void_p(-1).value

kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
create_file = kernel32.CreateFileW
create_file.argtypes = [
    wintypes.LPCWSTR,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    wintypes.LPVOID,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    wintypes.DWORD,
    wintypes.HANDLE,
]
create_file.restype = wintypes.HANDLE

handle = create_file(
    sys.argv[1],
    GENERIC_READ | GENERIC_WRITE,
    0,
    None,
    OPEN_ALWAYS,
    FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL,
    None,
)
if handle == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE:
    raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())

print("LOCKED", flush=True)
try:
    sys.stdin.buffer.read()
finally:
    kernel32.CloseHandle(handle)
```

Run `npm install`, then `npm start`. Keep the default filename, click **Save**, and observe the overwrite confirmation.

### Additional Information

Microsoft documents that a sharing violation should display an error and keep the save dialog open:

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/common-file-dialog#onshareviolation-and-onoverwrite

Electron's Windows implementation creates `IFileSaveDialog` with `FOS_OVERWRITEPROMPT` but does not register an `IFileDialogEvents::OnShareViolation` handler:

https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_win.cc

.NET WinForms contains a sharing-violation workaround because Windows can emit duplicate file-OK notifications for a write-locked target:

https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/blob/main/src/System.Windows.Forms/System/Windows/Forms/Dialogs/CommonDialogs/FileDialog.cs

nodes.title: [Bug]: Right-clicking a drag region in a window with no native title bar crashes the main process on macOS
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 42.0.1 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), arm64 (M5) ### What arch are you using? arm64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown — I've only tested 42.0.1. ### Expected Behavior Right-clicking a `-webkit-app-region: drag` region in a window with `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` should do nothing (or show a window menu), and certainly shouldn't terminate the app. ### Actual Behavior The main process segfaults immediately and the app dies. It's a null dereference in Chromium's views layer, reached straight from AppKit event dispatch: ``` Exception Type: EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV) Exception Subtype: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000000 Triggered by Thread: 0 CrBrowserMain, Dispatch Queue: com.apple.main-thread ``` Symbolicated against `electron-v42.0.1-darwin-arm64-symbols.zip` (the module UUID in the report matches the shipped framework), innermost frame first: ``` views::internal::RootView::UpdateCursor(ui::MouseEvent const&) <- crash views::internal::RootView::OnMouseReleased(ui::MouseEvent const&) views::Widget::OnMouseEvent(ui::MouseEvent*) -[BridgedContentView mouseEvent:] -[NativeWidgetMacNSWindow sendEvent:] -[ElectronNSWindow sendEvent:] -[NSApplication(NSEventRouting) sendEvent:] -[AtomApplication sendEvent:] -[NSApplication _handleEvent:] -[NSApplication run] ``` Registers at the fault: `far: 0x0`, `x8: 0x0`, `esr: 0x92000006 (Data Abort) byte read Translation fault`. `RootView::UpdateCursor` looks up a view for the event location and asks it for a cursor, so a null result from that lookup for a point in the drag region would produce exactly this. I haven't verified that specific line, though — that's inference from the stack rather than something I've confirmed. ### Testcase Gist URL Not a gist, but the whole reproduction is below. `package.json`: ```json { "name": "titlebar-rightclick-repro", "version": "1.0.0", "main": "main.js" } ``` `main.js`: ```js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron') app.whenReady().then(() => { const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 500, titleBarStyle: 'hidden', trafficLightPosition: { x: 12, y: 16 }, }) win.loadURL( 'data:text/html,' + encodeURIComponent(`
right-click anywhere in this strip

right-clicking below the strip is fine

`) ) }) ``` Run it, then right-click the dark strip. The app dies instantly, every time. ### Additional Information Right-clicking anywhere in the drag region crashes it, **including directly on the traffic-light buttons**. Right-clicking outside the drag region (the page content below) does not. I tried a few variations to narrow down what's needed. Both ingredients seem to be required — a drag region, in a window with no native title bar: | Window config | `-webkit-app-region: drag` present | Right-click in that region | | --- | --- | --- | | `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` | yes | **crash** | | default (framed) | yes | no crash | | `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` | no | no crash | | `frame: false` | yes | **crash** | With the default framed window I also right-clicked the real macOS title bar, which was fine. Worth noting that `frame: false` is affected too, not just `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` — the crash from that variant is identical to the `'hidden'` one across the entire stack, not just the inner frames. That probably widens the impact quite a bit, since custom chrome via `frame: false` is common. I found this because GitHub Desktop 3.6.3 — which uses a hidden title bar with a drag region — crashes whenever its title bar is right-clicked. I have seven crash reports from that app, all byte-identical to each other (same 25 frames, same image offsets), and the crash from the minimal repro above matches them exactly across the Electron/Chromium frames, with only the outer application frames differing as you'd expect. So the signature looks deterministic rather than a race. Since a bare Electron app reproduces it, this doesn't look app-specific, and presumably affects any Electron app using a drag-region title bar on this macOS version.

nodes.title: docs: clarify D3D11 synchronization contract for Windows OffscreenSharedTexture
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the contribution documentation for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the code of conduct that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for an issue that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.2.0

### Operating System

Windows 11 x64

### Description

The Windows `OffscreenSharedTexture` documentation describes `sharedTextureHandle` as a handle to a shared D3D11 texture and requires consumers to call `texture.release()` when finished. However, it does not describe the producer-to-consumer GPU synchronization guarantee at the time the `paint` event is emitted.

For ARGB/ABGR, Electron creates the resource with `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_NTHANDLE` and deliberately does not use `D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED_KEYEDMUTEX`:

https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v43.2.0/patches/chromium/osr_shared_texture_remove_keyed_mutex_on_win_dxgi.patch

An external native consumer currently follows this sequence:

```cpp
// The HANDLE is received from the paint event.
ComPtr<ID3D11Texture2D> texture;
device1->OpenSharedResource1(
    sharedTextureHandle,
    IID_PPV_ARGS(&texture));

// Read the texture on an external D3D11 device, for example:
context->CopyResource(destination.Get(), texture.Get());

// After the external operation is complete:
// texture.release() in Electron.
```

The JavaScript texture payload exposes no keyed-mutex key, fence, or sync token. The Chromium patch notes that Chromium will not write to the shared texture after its copy request returns, but it is not clear what guarantees that this GPU work is complete and visible to another D3D11 device when the JavaScript `paint` event is delivered.

### Questions

1. When the `paint` event is emitted, is the Windows ARGB/ABGR shared texture guaranteed to be immediately readable by another D3D11 device after `OpenSharedResource1`?
2. What synchronization or ordering primitive provides producer-to-consumer visibility in the mutex-free path?
3. If the external consumer must wait or synchronize before reading, what is the supported procedure?
4. Is keeping the texture object alive until the external GPU operation completes, followed by `texture.release()`, sufficient?

It would be helpful to document this contract in `offscreen-shared-texture.md`, because without it external D3D11 consumers cannot distinguish a supported read sequence from one that only happens to work on a particular driver.

### Expected Behavior

The documentation states the supported synchronization sequence and the point at which an external D3D11 consumer may safely read the shared texture.

### Actual Behavior

The handle type and release requirement are documented, but GPU read-readiness and cross-device synchronization are unspecified.

### Testcase Gist URL

N/A - this is a request to clarify the synchronization contract for the existing API.

nodes.title: [Docs]: corsEnabled has no documented meaning, and the GHSA-v3j7-r9gq-3gjw workaround describes it as doing the opposite
nodes.body:
### Preamble

**This is a documentation issue, not a vulnerability report.** The behaviour described below is
intended and covered by Electron's own tests — I confirmed that before opening this. The problem is
that the flag's meaning is undocumented, and the workaround text in a recently published advisory
describes it as doing the opposite of what it does.

### What's missing

`docs/api/structures/custom-scheme.md` lists every privilege with a description except `corsEnabled`:

```
* `corsEnabled` boolean (optional) - Default false.
```

There is nothing stating what it does. Given the name, a reader can reasonably assume "CORS is
enforced for this scheme". The actual behaviour is closer to the opposite: it **permits** cross-origin
fetches of the scheme, and no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` validation is performed on the response.

That reading is not a guess — it is what the test suite asserts (`spec/api-protocol-spec.ts`):

```js
it('does not affect cross-origin fetch to a corsEnabled scheme', async () => {
  protocol.handle('cors', () => new Response('ok'));   // no Access-Control-Allow-Origin
  await w.loadURL(remoteUrl);                          // a remote origin
  const body = await w.webContents.executeJavaScript("fetch('cors://host/').then(r => r.text())");
  expect(body).to.equal('ok');
});
```

plus `it('allows CORS requests by default')`, which expects `200` for the same scheme.

### Why it matters right now

The workaround section of [GHSA-v3j7-r9gq-3gjw](https://github.com/electron/electron/security/advisories/GHSA-v3j7-r9gq-3gjw)
(published 2026-07-27) says:

> Set `corsEnabled: true` on schemes that must enforce CORS

Read alongside the tests above, that advice points developers toward a configuration in which the
response body remains readable cross-origin. An app that serves sensitive data from a custom scheme
and follows the workaround may believe it has restricted reads when it has not.

The same section also suggests:

> validate the request `Origin` in your protocol handler before returning sensitive data

That one does not appear to be implementable on this path: the `protocol.handle` callback receives
`Origin: null` for these requests, so there is no origin available to validate. Logged from a handler
on 42.0.1:

```
[handler corson] request Origin header = null
```

### Reproduction

Measured on **42.0.1** (which contains the advisory's fix). A page on `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`
fetching a custom scheme whose handler returns a secret, varying only the ACAO header:

```
scheme registered { standard, secure, supportFetchAPI }              -> BLOCKED (expected, post-fix)
scheme registered { standard, secure, supportFetchAPI, corsEnabled } :
    no Access-Control-Allow-Origin                                   -> body readable, response.type "basic"
    Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://not-the-origin.example       -> body readable
    Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *                                    -> body readable
```

The mismatched-ACAO row is the informative one: the response is readable whether the header is
absent, wildcard, or names a different origin, so no validation is taking place. `response.type` is
`basic` rather than `cors`. Behaviour is the same on **41.3.0** (before the fix), so this is
longstanding and not a regression from it.

### Suggested changes

1. **Document `corsEnabled`.** Something like:

   > `corsEnabled` boolean (optional) - Whether cross-origin requests to this scheme are permitted.
   > When `true`, pages from other origins may `fetch()`/`XMLHttpRequest` this scheme and read the
   > response. Electron does not validate `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` for custom schemes, so this
   > grants access rather than enforcing the CORS protocol. Leave `false` for schemes serving data
   > that other origins should not read. Default false.

   (Wording is a starting point, not a proposal I'm attached to — the maintainers know the intent.)

2. **Amend the `GHSA-v3j7-r9gq-3gjw` workaround section**, since apps are acting on it now. If the
   goal is to prevent cross-origin reads, the advice is to leave `corsEnabled` unset (which the fix
   now enforces), not to enable it. And the `Origin`-validation suggestion needs either removal or a
   note that the header is not currently provided to handlers.

Happy to open a docs PR for (1) if that's useful. For (2) I assume amending a published advisory is
maintainer-only.

### Environment

* Electron: 42.0.1 and 41.3.0 (prebuilt, npm)
* Platform: macOS (darwin x64)

nodes.title: protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged accepts invalid scheme names
nodes.body:
### Description

`protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged()` does no validation of `customScheme.scheme` before registering it and forwarding it to child processes. Scheme names are joined with commas into the `--*-schemes` switches and split on commas on the renderer side, so a scheme string that isn't a valid RFC 3986 scheme (e.g. one containing a comma) is silently reinterpreted as multiple schemes in the renderer.

Relevant code: `RegisterSchemesAsPrivileged` in `shell/browser/api/electron_api_protocol.cc` pushes `custom_scheme.scheme` straight into the `url::Add*Scheme` calls and `AppendSchemesToCmdLine` without checking it; we already have `Browser::IsValidProtocolScheme` for exactly this.

### Expected behavior

Registering a scheme that isn't a valid scheme name throws, the same way `protocol.handle` does for invalid schemes.

### Actual behavior

The string is accepted; a comma-containing name shows up as two entries in the renderer's scheme lists.

### Testcase

```js
protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged([
  { scheme: 'foo,bar', privileges: { standard: true } }
]);
```

No error is thrown; in a renderer both `foo` and `bar` are registered as standard schemes.

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.2.0 (and any version using `@electron-internal/extract-zip`)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 26200, with Smart App Control **enforced** (`HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CI\Policy` → `VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState = 1`, `Win32_DeviceGuard.CodeIntegrityPolicyEnforcementStatus = 2`)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Two things:

1. When the bundled native extractor cannot be loaded, `install.js` should still be able to short-circuit via `isInstalled()` or `ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH` — i.e. the `require()` of the extractor should be lazy, so that users who already have a dist are not blocked by an extractor they never need.
2. When the native binding fails to load, the underlying error should be surfaced rather than replaced by an unrelated explanation.

### Actual Behavior

On a machine with Smart App Control enforced, the OS refuses to `dlopen` the bundled, unsigned `index.win32-x64-msvc.node`, so `npm install` never produces `dist/` or `path.txt`. Downstream this surfaces as e.g. electron-vite's `Error: Electron uninstall`.

**1. The failure is unrecoverable because the `require` is unconditional.**

```js
// node_modules/electron/install.js
5:  const { extract } = require('@electron-internal/extract-zip');   // <-- dies here
16: if (isInstalled()) { process.exit(0); }
73:   const electronPath = process.env.ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH || path.join(__dirname, 'dist', platformPath);
```

The module-level `require` on line 5 runs before `isInstalled()` (line 16) and before `ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH` is consulted (line 73). Per #52029, pointing `ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH` at an existing dist is supposed to make `install.js` bail early — but it cannot, because the process has already exited by then. There is no way to opt out of extraction.

**2. The reported cause is misleading.**

```
Error: Cannot find native binding. npm has a bug related to optional dependencies
(https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/4828). Please try `npm i` again after removing
both package-lock.json and node_modules directory.
  [cause]: Error: prebuild for this platform is not bundled
           (and @electron-internal/extract-zip-win32-x64-msvc is intentionally not published)
    cause: Error: An Application Control policy has blocked this file.
           \\?\...\@electron-internal\extract-zip\index.win32-x64-msvc.node
      code: 'ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED'
```

Only the innermost `cause` is the real reason. The top-level message is wrong in two ways:

- Following it (delete `node_modules` + `package-lock.json`, reinstall) does not change anything, and destroys the evidence.
- `@electron-internal/extract-zip` ships the `.node` files in the tarball (`files: ["index.*.node"]`) instead of using optional dependencies, so npm/cli#4828 cannot be the cause here. The file **is** present on disk (867,328 bytes) while the message claims the prebuild is "not bundled".

**3. It presents as a flaky install.** Smart App Control judges by reputation as well as signature, so this is not necessarily permanent. On the same machine, with SAC left enforced the whole time:

| local time | `process.dlopen` of that file |
|---|---|
| ~08:00 | blocked (`ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED`) |
| ~08:45 | loads fine |

So an affected user may see the install fail, retry later, succeed, and conclude the "remove `node_modules` and reinstall" advice worked — which makes the real cause very hard to find.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

The same code path can be reproduced deterministically without Smart App Control by making the binding unloadable, e.g. renaming `node_modules/@electron-internal/extract-zip/index.win32-x64-msvc.node`. `install.js` then fails at line 5 with the same top-level message.

For context, `electron.exe` itself and other unsigned native modules in the same tree (e.g. `node-pty`) were **not** blocked on this machine — only the extractor. Extracting the release zip with the OS-bundled `tar.exe` and writing `path.txt` manually produced a fully working install.

Suggested fixes, in order of value:

1. Make the extractor `require` lazy (move it into `extractFile()`), so `isInstalled()` and `ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH` can short-circuit before it is loaded.
2. In `binding.js`, when `dlopen` of a bundled `.node` fails with something other than "file not found", propagate that error instead of substituting the npm optional-dependencies message. As written, a permissions/policy failure is reported as a missing file.
3. Optionally, fall back to a JS-only extraction path when the native binding is unavailable.

Related: #52029 (`ELECTRON_OVERRIDE_DIST_PATH` ignored in `extract()`), #52099 and #51623 (other install failures caused by this module).

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

### Electron Version

43.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, GNOME, X11 (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11`)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

42.7.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Not directly testable: `BrowserWindow.setIgnoreMouseEvents()` is an Electron API.

### Expected Behavior

Calling `win.setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)` on a transparent, frameless, always-on-top window should restrict the native X11 input region so mouse clicks pass through to applications beneath the overlay.

With the minimal reproduction below on Electron 42.7.0, `XShapeGetRectangles(..., ShapeInput, ...)` reports:

```
input rectangles: 1
0: 1x1+0+0
```

Clicks pass through as expected.

### Actual Behavior

On Electron 43.2.0, the same window retains a full-window X11 input region:

```
input rectangles: 1
0: 400x400+0+0
```

For a full-screen overlay the reported region is the complete display (for example, `1919x1056`), so the transparent overlay blocks clicks to its own configuration window and every other application underneath it.

The result is unchanged when:

- Omitting the unsupported-on-Linux `{ forward: true }` option.
- Reapplying `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)` after `did-finish-load`.
- Setting `focusable` to either `true` or `false`.
- Setting `roundedCorners: false` (to rule out the Electron 43 Linux frameless-window change from #52111).
- Launching explicitly with `--ozone-platform=x11`.

Electron's `NativeWindowViews::SetIgnoreMouseEvents` X11 implementation appears source-identical between the 42 and 43 tags, so this may be a regression in the Chromium 148 to Chromium 150 platform/build stack.

### Testcase

Save as `main.cjs`, install the Electron version being tested, and run it with `npx electron main.cjs`. Try clicking a window beneath the red overlay.

```js
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron');

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  const win = new BrowserWindow({
    title: 'clickthrough-probe',
    width: 400,
    height: 400,
    x: 100,
    y: 100,
    transparent: true,
    frame: false,
    alwaysOnTop: true,
    focusable: false,
    roundedCorners: false,
  });

  win.setIgnoreMouseEvents(true);
  win.webContents.on('did-finish-load', () => {
    win.setIgnoreMouseEvents(true);
  });
  win.loadURL(
    'data:text/html,<body style="background:rgba(255,0,0,.2)"></body>',
  );
});

app.on('window-all-closed', () => {});
```

Version comparison:

```sh
npm install --save-dev electron@42.7.0
npx electron main.cjs  # click-through works

npm install --save-dev electron@43.2.0
npx electron main.cjs  # overlay blocks clicks
```

### Additional Information

This was found in a multi-display desktop overlay. The application-level workaround is to pin Electron 42.7.0:

https://github.com/Netroforge/hronomancer/commit/13fc4c77df14eef57e651c09ce10c9989951c3ed

Related but distinct:

- #16777 tracks support for the `forward` option on Linux. This reproduces without using `forward`.
- #51808 concerns native Wayland/Mutter; this reproduction is X11.
- #52452 is another Electron 43 Linux frameless-window regression. Disabling rounded corners does not fix this issue.

https://github.com/Netroforge/hronomancer/commit/007bf6fc72cbc55863a0f6e033a7516dba62aff7

Related but distinct:

- #16777 tracks support for the `forward` option on Linux. This reproduces without using `forward`.

nodes.title: [Bug]: Electron 43 bypasses native file-dialog directory persistence on all platforms
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a matching report.

### Electron Version

43.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows, macOS, and Linux

### Operating System Version

Windows 10/11; current macOS and Linux versions. On Linux, the effect depends on whether the active dialog backend honors `defaultPath`.

### What arch are you using?

x64 and arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

42.4.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No. This is in Electron's main-process `dialog` implementation.

### Expected Behavior

When an application omits `defaultPath`, Electron should preserve the pre-43 behavior and leave the initial directory to the native file dialog. This allows the OS to restore its persisted most-recently-used folder, including across application restarts.

### Actual Behavior

Since Electron 43, omitting `defaultPath` explicitly resolves to Downloads (or Home) on Windows, macOS, and Linux. This overrides or bypasses the native dialog's persisted directory whenever the platform backend honors the supplied path.

There is no API value that means “do not specify a default directory”: both an omitted and an empty `defaultPath` trigger the new fallback.

### Steps to reproduce

```js
const { app, dialog } = require('electron')

app.whenReady().then(() =>
  dialog.showOpenDialog({ properties: ['openDirectory'] })
)
```

1. Open the dialog and select a folder outside Downloads.
2. Open the dialog again, or restart the app and open it.
3. Electron 42 lets the native dialog restore the selected folder; Electron 43 opens Downloads again.

### Additional Information

This was introduced by #49868, which changed all three platform implementations:

- [Windows](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v43.2.0/shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_win.cc)
- [macOS](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v43.2.0/shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_mac.mm)
- [Linux](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v43.2.0/shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_linux.cc)

The previous behavior should be restored across all platforms when `defaultPath` is omitted. Applications that explicitly provide `defaultPath` should remain unchanged.

On Windows specifically, Electron calls [`IFileDialog::SetFolder`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v43.2.0/shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_win.cc#L107-L158). Microsoft documents that [`SetFolder`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/shobjidl_core/nf-shobjidl_core-ifiledialog-setfolder) overrides the most recently used folder regardless of previous user action. [`SetDefaultFolder`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/shobjidl_core/nf-shobjidl_core-ifiledialog-setdefaultfolder) would retain a Downloads fallback without overriding native MRU state; macOS and Linux should likewise avoid setting an initial directory when the application did not request one.

### Steps to reproduce


1. Open the dialog and select a folder outside Downloads, e.g. `D:\work`.
2. Open the dialog again, or restart the app and open it.
3. Electron 42 restores the selected folder; Electron 43 opens Downloads again.

### Additional Information

This was introduced by #49868. On Windows, Electron now resolves an omitted `defaultPath` to Downloads and calls [`IFileDialog::SetFolder`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v43.2.0/shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_win.cc#L107-L158).

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

An active Manifest V3 extension service worker that has registered a `chrome.storage.onChanged` listener should receive storage change events.

This should work regardless of whether the change originates from:

- an extension page
- an extension popup
- a content script
- the service worker itself

The behavior should match extension pages, popups, and content scripts, which receive these events correctly.

### Actual Behavior

In Electron 43.0.0, an active Manifest V3 service worker does not receive any `chrome.storage.onChanged` events.

I've tested these contexts:

| Receiver | Page write | Popup write | Content-script write | Service-worker write |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Extension page | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Popup | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Content script | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| MV3 service worker | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The writes all completed successfully. The other contexts each received exactly one event from every sender, while the service worker received none, including for its own write.

nodes.title: [Bug]: Linux systemd scope registration fails for app names needing escaping (StartTransientUnit InvalidArgs) — upstream fix available for backport
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.3.0 — but this affects all currently supported stable lines (41.x, 42.x, 43.x including latest stable 43.2.0). Already fixed on `main` via the Chromium 152 roll (see Additional Information).

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Arch Linux (kernel 7.0.12-arch1-1, x86_64), Wayland session (niri). Reproduces on any systemd-based Linux session, regardless of distro or compositor.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

N/A — this has been broken since `patches/chromium/fix_set_correct_app_id_on_linux.patch` started feeding real app/desktop names into Chromium's systemd scope registration.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes — the root cause is in Chromium code, and it is **already fixed in Chromium main** (see Additional Information). I am filing this against Electron to request picking the fix up for supported stable branches, since none of them contain it yet.

### Expected Behavior

Electron escapes the application name per `systemd.unit(5)` / `systemd-escape(1)` rules when constructing the transient scope unit name. For an app named `Open Design` the unit name should be `app-Open\x20Design-<pid>.scope`, `StartTransientUnit` succeeds, the browser process gets its systemd scope, and no error is logged.

### Actual Behavior

At every startup on a systemd-based Linux session, the browser process logs:

```
[29128:0725/174707.171989:ERROR:dbus/object_proxy.cc:572] Failed to call method: org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager.StartTransientUnit: object_path= /org/freedesktop/systemd1: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.InvalidArgs: Invalid unit name or type: app-Open Design-29128.scope
```

The scope is never created: the app's processes are not placed in a dedicated cgroup, and the XDG portal app-identification this registration exists for (`SetSystemdScopeUnitNameForXdgPortal`) is defeated. This affects any app whose name contains characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9:_]` — spaces are the most common case (e.g. `productName: "Open Design"`, which also becomes the packaged executable name).

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/arseniy-gl/bb764197b773bcf5abd79cccf1225ac9

(The gist sets `"desktopName": "Open Design.desktop"` in package.json so the repro also works unpackaged / in Fiddle; watch stderr on launch. With a packaged app, a `productName` containing a space is sufficient on its own.)

### Additional Information

Root-cause chain:

1. `shell/browser/api/electron_api_app.cc` — `App::SetDesktopName()` sets the `CHROME_DESKTOP` env var (from `packageJson.desktopName` or `<executable basename>.desktop`, see `lib/browser/init.ts`).
2. `patches/chromium/fix_set_correct_app_id_on_linux.patch` makes `version_info::nix::GetAppName()` return the `CHROME_DESKTOP` basename **verbatim** (e.g. `Open Design`).
3. Chromium `components/dbus/xdg/systemd.cc` (`OnNameHasOwnerResponse`) builds the unit name with the format `app-$1-$2.scope` and substitutes the app name **without escaping**: [systemd.cc @ 146.0.7680.188 (Electron 41.3.0)](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/146.0.7680.188/components/dbus/xdg/systemd.cc#:~:text=ReplaceStringPlaceholders). systemd unit names may only contain ASCII alphanumerics, `:`, `_`, `.`, `-`; anything else must be `\xNN`-escaped, so systemd rejects the call with `InvalidArgs`.

Fixed upstream: Chromium commit [`7becfc78c4fabdffac412e894fd6ba2c92b7c804`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/commit/7becfc78c4fabdffac412e894fd6ba2c92b7c804) "Escape systemd unit name for XDG portal" ([crrev.com/c/8127836](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8127836), [crbug 530704654](https://issues.chromium.org/530704654), landed 2026-07-20) adds `internal::EscapeSystemdUnitName()` implementing exactly the `systemd-escape(1)` rules. I verified its presence/absence per branch:

| Electron | Chromium | `EscapeSystemdUnitName` present? |
|---|---|---|
| 41.3.0 | 146.0.7680.188 | ❌ |
| 42.x | 148.0.7778.96 | ❌ |
| 43.2.0 (latest stable) | 150.0.7871.46 | ❌ |
| `main` | 152.0.7965.0 | ✅ |

So the fix will reach Electron naturally with the Chromium 152 line, but every supported stable branch is affected until then.

**Request:** please consider backporting the upstream fix to the supported stable lines (43-x-y, 42-x-y, 41-x-y). It is small and self-contained (one new helper + one call site), and it unbreaks systemd scope registration — and the portal app identification built on it — for every Electron app with a space (or other escapable character) in its name.
